prs.title: Add tone mapping to canvas
prs.author: ccameron-chromium
prs.body:
Add tone mapping to canvas

Add the `CanvasToneMapping` dictionary and `CanvasToneMappingMode` enum (`"standard"` and `"extended"`), and a `toneMapping` member to `CanvasRenderingContext2DSettings`, reflected by `getContextAttributes()`. These replace WebGPU's `GPUCanvasToneMapping` and `GPUCanvasToneMappingMode`, which WebGPU will reference from HTML in the same way it references `PredefinedColorSpace`.

When a canvas is rendered to the output device, it is now tone mapped to the device's HDR headroom, as limited by `dynamic-range-limit`, before color space conversion.

This has been the planned trajectory of the API since [its proposal to WebGPU](https://github.com/ccameron-chromium/webgpu-hdr/blob/main/EXPLAINER.md#notes-on-canvasrenderingcontext2d-and-unification-of-apis). Its move from WebGPU-only to HTML was waiting for float16 support for 2D canvas and WebGL.

Fixes https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11424

prs.title: Refine when selectedcontent elements are updated
prs.author: annevk
prs.body:
This is a follow-up to #12263 that addresses the remaining cases where selectedcontent elements were updated too little or too much:

* Inserting an option element that causes another option element to become selected now updates selectedcontent elements. This happens when the select element has no selected option, e.g., after setting selectedIndex to -1.
* Inserting a select element that already contains option elements now updates its selectedcontent elements once, rather than again from the post-connection steps of its selected option element.
* Inserting a selectedcontent element before option elements that change selectedness now updates it once, rather than from both its own post-connection steps and those of the option elements. Its post-connection steps now leave updating it to its select element's pending selectedcontent update, if there is one.
* The microtasks queued to update selectedcontent elements after option elements are removed or moved are now coalesced per select element, and do nothing if the selectedcontent elements were updated in the meantime.
* Moving a selectedcontent element now queues the same update for its select element, rather than a microtask that updates the moved element from that select element even if it was moved out of it by the time the microtask runs. This also updates the select element's other selectedcontent elements.
* Moving a selectedcontent element no longer updates it when its select element and disabledness do not change, e.g.

prs.author: JinDX
prs.body: Use `SharedWorkerOptions` when a string is supplied as the second argument to `SharedWorker()`. This gives the legacy name overload the same `extendedLifetime: false` default as the dictionary overload, which the subsequent reuse check and initialization both read. The existing [shared worker name test](workers/shared-worker-name-via-options.html) exercises reusing a worker across the two overloads. *** /workers.html ( diff )

prs.title: Bind the navigation API method tracker when aborting a NavigateEvent
prs.author: JinDX
prs.body: Read the ongoing API method tracker into `apiMethodTracker` in the steps to abort a `NavigateEvent`. The existing step checks that tracker for null and then passes an unbound `apiMethodTracker` to the promise rejection algorithm. The new binding supplies the checked tracker at the same point in the steps. The existing [stop test](navigation-api/ordering-and-transition/navigate-intercept-stop.html) and [interception rejection test](navigation-api/ordering-and-transition/navigate-same-document-intercept-reject.html) both assert that the navigation result’s `finished` promise rejects after the `committed` promise has been fulfilled. *** /nav-history-apis.html ( diff )

prs.title: Define when the parser finishes parsing an element's children
prs.author: annevk
prs.body:
Define when the parser finishes parsing an element's children

Define "finish parsing the children" of an element, which runs whenever
an element leaves the stack of open elements: when it is popped, when
it is removed without being the current node (the "form" end tag, the
head element pointer, and the adoption agency algorithm), and when the
adoption agency algorithm replaces its entry. This replaces the
scattered "when a foo element is popped off the stack of open elements
of an HTML parser or XML parser" prose with "HTML element children
parsed steps", keyed on local name alongside the existing insertion,
post-connection, removing, and moving steps.

Running these steps when an element is removed without being the
current node matches WebKit and Chromium. Gecko only runs them when the
element is popped.

The style, audio/video, option, and textarea prose is migrated to the
new hook. The object element's condition list keeps its own wording, as
formalizing it means parameterizing the ~390-line algorithm that
determines what an object element represents.

"Update a style block" now takes the style element as an argument.

Tests: https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/64990.

Closes #11781.
